ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (34) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

The Sermon on the Mount is translated from the Russian as printed, with lowercase 'father' for «отец» (otets) and 'do not resist evil' for «не противься злому» (ne protiv'sya zlomu) (D0002); «мытари» (mytari) are 'tax collectors' and «язычники» (yazychniki) 'pagans'. The verse 'love your enemies…' (Matthew 5:44) stands in the source after the reference line, outside the quotation, and is kept in that position. Tolstoy's own reference «Левит 19, 17—18» (Levit 19, 17–18, 'Leviticus 19:17–18') for 'hate your enemy' is kept as printed.

Source observation: [21] Matthew 5:44 («А я говорю вам: любите врагов ваших…», A ya govoryu vam: lyubite vragov vashikh, 'But I say to you: love your enemies…') is printed after the reference line [20], unquoted, instead of between [15] and [16] where it belongs; translated in place as printed
